column1: In Photoshop/After Effects compositing, what does the Multiply blend mode formula do mathematically, and what is its key visual property?
column2: result = base × blend (normalized 0–1). Since both values are ≤1, the result can never be brighter than either input — Multiply always darkens. Used for shadows and grounding objects.

column1: Why does painting on a 50% gray layer set to Overlay blend mode add contrast invisibly until you paint on it?
column2: Overlay pivots at 50% gray: it applies Multiply on the dark half and Screen on the light half of the blend layer. Pure 50% gray is the exact pivot point, so it contributes nothing — only deviation from gray darkens or lightens the image.

column1: How does a layer mask mathematically affect compositing in Photoshop?
column2: A mask is a grayscale channel where white = 100% opacity, black = 0%, gray = partial. The engine multiplies the layer's existing alpha by the mask value before compositing — it's one multiplication operation, however the grayscale map was generated (feathering, gradients, luminosity selections).

column1: What is the architectural difference between a 'linked' and an 'embedded' asset across Creative Cloud apps, and why does it matter?
column2: A linked asset stores only a path/GUID reference plus a low-res proxy for display; an embedded asset copies the data in. Linking lets 'Edit Original' reopen the exact source app and layer stack, so edits upstream propagate everywhere downstream without re-exporting — flattening or embedding breaks this edit graph.

column1: In vector path construction, what do a Bézier anchor point's handle direction and handle length each control?
column2: Handle direction sets the tangent direction of the curve at that anchor; handle length sets how long the curve 'obeys' that tangent before bending away toward the next anchor.

column1: What are the three anchor point types in Illustrator and their defining handle configurations?
column2: Corner: no handles, sharp angle. Smooth: two handles, symmetrical and locked opposite each other, continuous flowing curve. Cusp/combination: two independent handles (different angle/length), curve changes direction sharply at the anchor.

column1: Why can vector files like Illustrator logos scale from a business card to a billboard with no quality loss?
column2: The shape is stored as a small set of numbers (anchor point positions and handle offsets), not as pixels, so the renderer recomputes the exact same curve mathematically at any output resolution — no blur or stair-stepping.

column1: In InDesign, why should baseline grid increment be set to match body text leading (e.g., 14pt for 10/14pt body text)?
column2: Setting the increment equal to the leading ensures every paragraph style whose leading is a multiple of that value (14, 28, 42pt...) locks cleanly to the grid, keeping text aligned across columns even when font sizes differ.

column1: What happens to readability if line leading drops below 120% of point size, versus rising above 150%?
column2: Below 120% leading, lines visually fuse and the eye re-reads words. Above 150%, the eye loses the line on the return sweep. The comfortable range (120–145%) matches natural saccade length.

column1: What are the three interpolation families between After Effects keyframes, and what motion does each produce?
column2: Linear: constant velocity, mechanical/robotic. Bezier/Ease: velocity ramps up and down (ease-in/ease-out), mimicking real-world acceleration/deceleration. Hold: no interpolation — value snaps at the next keyframe, used for discrete state changes or stop-motion looks.

column1: In After Effects, once you've clicked the stopwatch icon to arm keyframing on a property, how do you create additional keyframes?
column2: Simply move the playhead to a new time and change the property's value — AE automatically creates a new keyframe; you do not need to click the stopwatch again.

column1: Why can a PSD tagged with Adobe RGB look different when brought into a Premiere project set to Rec.709?
column2: Color management (the color profile) travels with the file as metadata, but if the receiving app's project color space doesn't match the source profile, colors shift — profile mismatches are the most common cause of cross-app color discrepancies.
